confirmed.title: Public repo with no CI secret scanning — the control gap that let SECR-01 live 9 months
confirmed.evidence: The repo is public (`gh repo view` -> visibility PUBLIC, MIT LICENSE, created 2025-11-29). CI has five gates wired in `.github/workflows/supabase-preview.yml` — `migration-check` (l.40), `migration-security` (l.62, correctly invoking `scripts/ci/check-migration-security.mjs` at l.78), `lint` (l.80), `vitest` (l.110), `build` (l.125) — but `grep -rlniE 'gitleaks|trufflehog|secret.scan|detect-secrets' .github/ scripts/ci/` returns nothing. There is no pre-commit hook or CI job that would reject a committed credential. `.gitignore` correctly covers `.env*` and `*.pem` and `.env.local` is untracked (verified: `git ls-files | grep -iE '\.env'` returns only `.env.example`), so the ONLY thing that stopped further leakage was that developers happened to use env vars — SECR-01 shows that convention failing silently. Separately, commit b5d965f6 (2026-04-08) committed 1773 build-artifact files (`.next-old/cache/webpack/*.pack.gz`, `.claude/worktrees/*`) into the public history; these are gone from HEAD (`git ls-files | grep -cE '^(\.next|\.claude|\.next-old)/'` -> 0) and I confirmed by regex scan that they contain no real GitHub PAT, AWS AKID, or service_role JWT — but they are exactly the class of blob that inlines build-time env.
confirmed.consequence: Public visibility converts every future credential slip into an immediate internet-wide disclosure with zero delay and no detection. Since the repo also publishes the full schema, all migrations, and every RLS policy, an attacker who obtains any credential in future has a complete map to exploit it. The absence of a scanner means the next SECR-01 is equally likely to sit undetected for months.
confirmed.remediation: Decide deliberately whether public is intended for a proprietary client-financial-data platform; if not, flip the repo to private (this does not remediate SECR-01 — the key must still be revoked, as forks/clones/caches persist). Either way, add a secret-scanning gate: enable GitHub Secret Scanning + Push Protection (free on public repos, and the single highest-value control here), and add a `gitleaks`/`trufflehog` job to `supabase-preview.yml` alongside the existing `migration-security` job so PRs are blocked on credential-shaped diffs. Add `.next*/` and `.claude/worktrees/` guards to the same gate to stop build-cache commits.

1. "There is no pre-commit hook or CI job that would reject a committed credential" is false at the platform layer. `gh api repos/.../  --jq .security_and_analysis` returns: secret_scanning ENABLED, secret_scanning_push_protection ENABLED. Only `secret_scanning_non_provider_patterns` and `secret_scanning_validity_checks` are disabled (and `dependabot_security_updates` disabled).

2. "The absence of a scanner means the next SECR-01 is equally likely to sit undetected for months" is directly falsified by the data. A scanner DID detect SECR-01, ~6 seconds after repo creation: `gh api repos/.../secret-scanning/alerts` -> alert #1, secret_type "supabase_service_key", created_at 2025-11-29T09:54:10Z, state "open", publicly_leaked true, multi_repo true, push_protection_bypassed FALSE. Detection was never the failure. The alert has simply sat open and untriaged for 9 months. The corrected root cause of SECR-01's longevity is an unmonitored GitHub Security tab / no alert routing + no key rotation — a process gap, not a tooling gap. Adding gitleaks to CI would not have changed the outcome by one day.

3. The finder's own evidence undercuts itself: it reports scanning the b5d965f6 build artifacts and finding "no real ... service_role JWT". A real, live service_role JWT is sitting in a currently-TRACKED file at HEAD — /Users/mattmalouf/Desktop/business-coaching-platform/scripts/run-payroll-migration.js:5-6 (`supabaseUrl = 'https://uudfstpvndurzwnapibf.supabase.co'`, `supabaseKey = 'eyJ...role":"service_role"...'`, exp 2069). ACTION NOTE for the parent: the materially urgent item surfaced here belongs to SECR-01, not SECR-02 — secret-scanning alert #1 is still `state: open` with the service_role JWT live in a tracked file at HEAD of a public repo. Rotating the key and purging/removing scripts/run-payroll-migration.js is the fix; enabling non-provider patterns + validity checks is the LOW follow-up that is the true content of SECR-02.

confirmed.title: Consolidated cashflow runs the SAME business-wide forecast once per tenant and then SUMS them — every cash movement is multiplied by the tenant count (Dragon = 2×, live)
confirmed.evidence:
buildConsolidatedCashflow (cashflow.ts:428-515) loads ONE business-level baseline via loadBusinessBaseline (line 409) and then, inside `tenants.map(...)`, calls `generateCashflowForecast(baseline.plLines, baseline.payrollSummary, tenantAssumptions, baseline.forecast, baseline.plannedSpends, ...)` (line 447) for EVERY tenant. The only per-tenant difference is `opening_bank_balance` (line 444) — plLines, payroll, planned spends and all other assumptions are identical. combineMemberForecasts (line 348-393) then does `combinedMonths[idx].cash_in += mm.cash_in; cash_out += mm.cash_out; net_movement += mm.net_movement` (lines 373-375) across every tenant, and threads the running balance from that sum (lines 381-386).

Recomputation: for a business with T tenants and a baseline month net movement N_m, consolidated net_movement[m] = T·N_m, and consolidated closing = Σopening_t + Σ_m T·N_m. The module header (lines 29-33) admits the baseline is "intentionally duplicated ... for cash_in / cash_out / net_movement" but the combine step sums the duplicates instead of taking one copy.

Prod reachability: SELECT on financial_forecasts shows Dragon Roofing (business_profiles.id a1657c67-a12f-41e0-a312-ba90180e864b) has an ACTIVE FY2027 forecast 7b90633d-466b-46bc-bbfd-fa20b27f98f1 with 68 forecast_pl_lines, and xero_connections shows Dragon has 2 active include_in_consolidation tenants (Dragon Roofing Pty Ltd + EASY HAIL CLAIM PTY LTD). So the Consolidated Cashflow tab (wired at src/app/finances/monthly-report/page.tsx:1470) renders exactly 2× Dragon's real forecast cash in/out today. No banner, no diagnostic flags the multiplication — diagnostics.notes (cashflow.ts:417-423) only mentions the shared baseline, not the double-count.
confirmed.consequence: Dragon Roofing's consolidated 12-month cashflow shows double the real receipts, double the real payments, and a year-end closing bank balance inflated by one extra full year of net cash movement. A coach reading it would give a client a cash-runway number that is off by 100% of the year's net movement. Scales with tenant count (IICT would be 3×).
confirmed.remediation: Run the shared baseline ONCE, not per tenant. Either (a) build the consolidated series from a single generateCashflowForecast call and use per-tenant openings only to split the opening balance, or (b) split forecast_pl_lines per tenant (the TODO at cashflow.ts:31) before summing. Until fixed, refuse to render the consolidated column for businesses with >1 tenant and no tenant-scoped forecast, rather than showing a multiplied total.

No interest-on-balance, no overdraft feedback. So every tenant's `cash_in`, `cash_out`, `net_movement` series is BIT-IDENTICAL.

1. "IICT would be 3×" — IICT has NO active forecast (both its FY2027 forecasts, 88199866… and 1c72355f…, are is_active=false). `loadBusinessBaseline` returns null, so IICT's tab renders all-zero months plus the "No active forecast found" note (cashflow.ts:411-415). Today exactly ONE business (Dragon) is affected, not two.
2. The surface is NOT client-facing. `canSeeConsolidated = isConsolidationGroup === true && userRole !== 'client'` (page.tsx:249), the route hard-403s non-coach/admin (route.ts:100-107), and page.tsx:251-253 bounces a client off a persisted consolidated tab. A client sees the wrong figure only if a coach reads it off the screen and relays it.

So: a live, unconditional, silently-wrong money number on a real coach-facing report surface for a ~$10M client — squarely HIGH ("wrong numbers under a reachable condition", and here the condition is just opening the tab). It falls short of CRITICAL because it is not client-facing, involves no data loss or breach, and touches a forward forecast view rather than a reported actual. The fix is required regardless: the combine must take ONE copy of the shared baseline's movements (or the module must refuse to render a "Consolidated" row until forecast_pl_lines is tenant-scoped), and per-tenant openings should keep summing as they already correctly do.

confirmed.title: financial_metrics.total_cash is 0.00 in every row fleet-wide — /cfo shows "Cash $0" for every client, and "Reconciled" for every client

confirmed.title: Reconciliation route fails open to "All transactions reconciled" for the two multi-org businesses (Dragon Roofing, IICT Group) because .maybeSingle() nulls on >1 connection
confirmed.evidence:
Prod data: `select business_id, count(*) from xero_connections where is_active group by 1` — Dragon Roofing (businesses.id c7df2983-5711-4959-8ec8-a48030d62666) has 2 active connections (Dragon Roofing Pty Ltd, EASY HAIL CLAIM PTY LTD); IICT Group (fbc6dffd-677d-47ec-8277-7157982938e7) has 3 (IICT Group Pty Ltd, IICT (Aust) Pty Ltd, IICT Group Limited). src/app/api/Xero/reconciliation/route.ts:72, :76, :80 — all three dual-ID fallbacks use `.eq('business_id', …).eq('is_active', true).maybeSingle()` and destructure only `{ data }`. node_modules/@supabase/postgrest-js/dist/cjs/PostgrestBuilder.js:108-121 sets `data = null` and returns PGRST116 whenever a maybeSingle GET returns more than one row. The error is discarded, so `connection` stays null through all three attempts for exactly these two businesses.

route.ts:83-91 then returns `{ unreconciled_count: 0, unreconciled_total: 0, is_clean: true, no_connection: true }`.

Consumers ignore `no_connection`: src/app/finances/monthly-report/components/ReconciliationGate.tsx:34 renders the green "All transactions reconciled for <Month>" banner on `is_clean`; src/app/finances/monthly-report/page.tsx:725 computes `const isDraft = forceDraft || (reconciliation ? !reconciliation.is_clean : false)` — so the generated report is stamped FINAL rather than DRAFT.

A CFO-grade control fails open to "clean" on the exact clients it matters most for, and the cashflow CapEx tab silently returns empty for them.
confirmed.remediation: Replace the three-step `.maybeSingle()` fallback with the existing multi-tenant helper `resolveXeroConnections` (src/lib/business/resolveXeroBusinessId.ts:46-88, whose header already notes "Dragon Roofing has 2, IICT Group has 3"), loop the BankTransactions query over every returned connection, and sum. Until then, at minimum destructure and check the PostgREST error, and never return `is_clean: true` when no connection was resolved — return an explicit unknown state that ReconciliationGate renders amber and that forces DRAFT.

Every load-bearing claim survives adversarial verification; two details corrected, one strengthened, plus new corroborating prod evidence.

PostgrestTransformBuilder.js:121-132 confirms maybeSingle on GET sets Accept:application/json and `isMaybeSingle=true`. So `data` is null and the discarded `error` is the only signal.

BOTH ID-SPACES DEAD-END — verified by recomputation, not assumed. If the caller passes businesses.id: path 1 matches 2–3 rows → null; path 2 queries xero_connections by business_profiles.id (wrong id-space) → 0 rows; path 3 looks up business_profiles WHERE id = a businesses.id → no match. confirmed.title: mirror_freshness invariant measures the newest period LABEL, not when data was last written — it cannot detect a mid-month pipeline death

confirmed.consequence: The one daily check whose stated job is 'is the mirror serving current numbers' returns PASS for a tenant whose pipe has been dead for half a month, and would keep returning PASS for up to ~60 days (until the label falls 3 months behind). It is a check that reads the same whether the pipe is alive or dead — the exact failure mode the cron's own header comment says it exists to prevent. Every future mid-month sync death is invisible to it.
confirmed.remediation: Compute freshness from ingest time, not the period label: add a second observed value = hours since max(xero_pl_lines.updated_at) for the tenant, and fail when it exceeds ~2 sync cadences (e.g. 30h). verdict.reasoning:
CODE CLAIM: CONFIRMED verbatim. src/app/api/cron/metric-invariants/route.ts:244-257 is exactly as quoted — `const plMonth = newestMonthKey(pl); const monthsBehind = plMonth ? monthsBetween(plMonth, now) : null; ... passed: monthsBehind !== null && monthsBehind <= FRESHNESS_MAX_MONTHS_BEHIND` with FRESHNESS_MAX_MONTHS_BEHIND = 2 (line 45). newestMonthKey (line 73) scans the KEYS of monthly_values; monthsBetween (line 84) is pure calendar arithmetic on that label. Nothing in the check reads updated_at, last_synced_at, or sync_jobs — so it is structurally incapable of distinguishing "August written this morning" from "August written on the 11th and never again".

PROD CLAIM: CONFIRMED, re-run read-only. metric_invariant_runs run_at 2026-08-26 05:00:26 — mirror_freshness / 'Armstrong & Co Projects Pty Ltd' / passed=true / observed=0 / detail 'newest P&L month in mirror: 2026-08'. NOT a duplicate of the four already-audited areas.

refuted.title: Quarterly variance % divides by a signed denominator — a negative forecast (loss-making quarter) flips the sign, showing a beat as a miss
refuted.evidence:
`function calcVariancePct(forecast, actual) { if (forecast === 0) return 0; return Math.round(((actual - forecast) / forecast) * 100) }` (lines 182-185). No Math.abs on the denominator — unlike every sibling in the codebase (src/lib/monthly-report/shared.ts:47, full-year/route.ts:399, generate/route.ts:587 all use `/ Math.abs(budget)`). It is applied to grossProfit (line 207) and netProfit (line 219), both of which are routinely negative.

Recomputation with real prod data: forecast 6e493c8c-9888-4f4b-9671-e7a08afc467a (is_active) has monthly forecast net profit of -100,435.83 (2026-10), -167,220.83 (2026-11), -102,208.83 (2026-12) → Q2 FY2027 npForecast = -369,865.49. If the client halves the loss and posts npActual = -184,932, calcVariancePct = ((-184,932) - (-369,865.49)) / (-369,865.49) × 100 = 184,933.49 / -369,865.49 × 100 = -50%. The client beat the plan by $184,933 and the quarterly review renders -50%. Dragon Roofing's active forecast 7b90633d also has negative NP months (2026-08: -42,723; 2026-10: -69,651; 2027-01: -38,489).

Consumed by src/app/quarterly-review/components/steps/ConfidenceRealignmentStep.tsx:214, which feeds data.grossProfit and data.netProfit straight into the client-facing quarterly review.
refuted.consequence: In any quarter where the budgeted gross profit or net profit is negative, the quarterly review shows the sign of the variance percentage inverted: a client who cut their loss in half is told they are 50% behind plan, and a client whose loss doubled is told they are 50% ahead. This drives the 'adjust remaining forecast months' decision in the same step.
refuted.remediation: Change to `((actual - forecast) / Math.abs(forecast)) * 100`, matching shared.ts:47. Add a unit test with a negative forecast asserting a smaller loss yields a positive percentage.

verdict.reasoning:
The quoted code exists exactly as described — src/app/api/forecast/quarterly-summary/route.ts:182-185 is `function calcVariancePct(forecast, actual) { if (forecast === 0) return 0; return Math.round(((actual - forecast) / forecast) * 100) }` with no Math.abs on the denominator, and it is applied to grossProfit (line 207) and netProfit (line 219). The arithmetic in the finder's example is also correct: the API would return variancePct = -50 for npForecast -369,865.49 / npActual -184,932.

The claimed consequence is nevertheless unreachable, because the only consumer never uses the sign the API returns.

Consumer trace (exhaustive): a repo-wide grep for `quarterly-summary` outside the route itself returns only .planning/*.md docs and ONE code site — src/app/quarterly-review/components/steps/ConfidenceRealignmentStep.tsx:214. The response is stored in local state (`setForecastVariance`, lines 219-226) and used in exactly two places: `forecastVariance.forecastId` for the adjust-forward POST (line 437), and the Forecast vs Actuals table (lines 540-557). It is never persisted, never fed to an AI prompt, never re-derived.

The table renders each row as:
  src/.../ConfidenceRealignmentStep.tsx:552-554 → `className={getVarianceColor(row.variance)}` … `{formatVariance(row.variance, row.variancePct)}`
and the formatter (lines 466-472) is:
  `const pctStr = `${Math.abs(variancePct)}%`;`
  `if (variance > 0) return `+${absFormatted} +${pctStr}`;`
  `if (variance < 0) return `(${absFormatted}) -${pctStr}`;`

So the displayed sign is taken from `variance` (= actual − forecast, computed at route.ts:206/218 and always sign-correct) and the percentage is Math.abs'd. Because |x / y| === |x| / |y|, the rendered string is byte-identical to what a `/ Math.abs(forecast)` denominator would produce. Recomputing the finder's own scenario end-to-end: variance = −184,932 − (−369,865.49) = +184,933.49 > 0, variancePct = −50 → Math.abs → 50, sign from variance → the UI renders "+$184,933 +50%" in green (getVarianceColor, line 461: variance > 0 → text-green-600). The client who halved their loss is shown a beat, not a −50% miss. The doubled-loss case renders "($X) −Y%" in red, also correct. The colour is likewise driven by `variance`, not by the pct.

Note also that the only three rows rendered are revenue, grossProfit, netProfit — cogs and opex (where a positive variance would be bad-but-green) are not displayed at all.

Residual (INFO, hygiene only): the raw API contract is still inconsistent with its siblings (src/lib/monthly-report/shared.ts:47, forecast full-year/route.ts:399, generate/route.ts:587 all divide by Math.abs(budget)), so a second consumer that trusted `variancePct`'s sign — or displayed it without the Math.abs/`variance`-sign wrapper — would render inverted percentages for loss-making quarters. That is a latent trap worth a one-line fix (add Math.abs to the denominator, a no-op for the current UI), not a live wrong client-facing number.

Downstream: useCashflowForecast.ts:220 auto-fires the sync whenever opening_bank_balance === 0, so it retries and 400s every load; the engine then runs with `let bankBalance = assumptions.opening_bank_balance` = 0 (src/lib/cashflow/engine.ts:493).

Secondary defect: even if the maybeSingle were fixed to take one row, a single-connection pick would source the opening balance from ONE Xero org for a 2-3 org group — under-reporting group cash.

A banner exists (CashflowForecastTab.tsx:148) so it is not fully silent, but the feature is unusable for exactly the two clients who most need consolidated cash visibility.
rest.remediation: Replace the three maybeSingle() lookups with a single `.in('business_id', ids.all).eq('is_active', true)` list query using resolveBusinessProfileIds, then sum the Balance Sheet across ALL returned connections (translating non-AUD orgs) rather than picking one. At minimum, stop swallowing the PGRST116 error so the multi-org case is visible in Sentry.

rest.title: Consolidation dedup keys on account_name alone while the alignment key is account_type::account_name — same-named accounts of different types would be merged into one, moving money between P&L sections
rest.evidence:
deduplicateLines uses `const key = line.account_name` (line 34) and sums monthly_values into the FIRST row seen (lines 41-43), keeping that row's account_type. But accountAlignmentKey (line 24) is `${account_type}::${account_name}`, and the module header explicitly states the invariant: 'Two accounts with the same display name but different account_type (e.g. "Bank Fees" as opex vs other_expense) stay separate rows' (lines 9-10, Pitfall 4). deduplicateLines is called before buildAlignedAccountUniverse (engine.ts:576-579, 686-689), so it silently violates the invariant the rest of the module is built around.

Effect if it fires: the merged row lands under the first-seen account_type; the other type's universe row is zero-filled by buildEntityColumn (lines 111-126). If the first-seen type were 'revenue' and the duplicate 'opex', the opex amount is added to revenue and the opex row shows $0.

Currently latent — `SELECT business_id, tenant_id, account_name, count(distinct account_type) FROM xero_pl_lines_wide_compat GROUP BY 1,2,3 HAVING count(distinct account_type) > 1` returns zero rows today. (The 2-rows-per-account duplicates that DO exist for Dragon — e.g. 'Sales - Deposit' and 'Bank Fees' on tenant 3b67e5b6 — are same-type and hold non-overlapping month keys (2025-04..06 vs 2025-07..2026-08), so the summing merge is currently harmless.)
rest.consequence: No live impact today, but a single Xero re-classification (or a chart-of-accounts edit that maps one name to two types across the FY boundary) would silently move an expense amount into revenue in the consolidated P&L, with no error and no diagnostic. This is a latent CFO-accuracy landmine on the multi-entity path.
rest.remediation: Change deduplicateLines' key to `accountAlignmentKey(line)` so it agrees with the universe key, and add a test with two same-named lines of different account_type asserting they survive as two rows.

rest.title: Intercompany eliminations are applied ONLY to the report month — every other month of the consolidated P&L (and any YTD/FY total built from it) is un-eliminated
rest.evidence:
applyEliminations resolves each rule against `line.monthly_values[reportMonth]` only (eliminations.ts:112, 126). combineTenants then applies them under `if (m === reportMonth)` (engine.ts:259-262); every other month in fyMonths is a raw cross-tenant sum with no elimination. The consolidated FY row and any YTD derived from consolidated.lines therefore contain full intercompany revenue and expense for 11 of 12 months.

Separately, `SELECT * FROM consolidation_elimination_rules` returns ZERO rows in prod — so IICT Group (3 orgs: IICT (Aust) Pty Ltd, IICT Group Pty Ltd, IICT Group Limited) and Dragon Roofing (2 orgs) currently have NO intercompany eliminations configured at all, in any month. The engine reports eliminations_applied_count: 0 (engine.ts:769) but nothing in the UI distinguishes 'nothing to eliminate' from 'nobody configured it'.
rest.consequence: Consolidated group revenue for IICT and Dragon includes any inter-entity trading at full value, in every month. Even once rules are configured, only the single report month would be corrected — the 12-month consolidated view and any FY total would still double-count. Neither state is disclosed to the reader.
rest.remediation: (1) Apply eliminations across all fyMonths, not just reportMonth (change eliminations.ts to accept a month list and combineTenants to look up per-month entries). (2) Surface a diagnostic/banner when a business has 2+ consolidation tenants and zero active elimination rules, so 'unconfigured' is visibly different from 'nothing to eliminate'.

rest.title: A partially-elapsed month's OXR average is written under the month-start period key and never re-derived, so a mid-month sync permanently freezes an incomplete monthly average
rest.evidence:
deriveMonthlyRatePair enumerates calendar days 'cap at today' (oxr.ts:125) and computes `monthly_average = sum / dailyRates.length` over whatever days were fetched (oxr.ts:192-193), throwing only if fewer than 5 days succeeded (line 186). The route then writes `period: `${year}-${month}-01`` (route.ts:138) and upserts on (currency_pair, rate_type, period) (line 158). Nothing marks the row as partial, and nothing re-runs it once the month completes — the only writer is this manual admin endpoint.

Prod: the HKD/AUD monthly_average for 2026-05 is stored at period 2026-05-01 with source 'oxr', and its sibling closing_spot is dated 2026-05-25 — proving the May sync ran on 25 May, i.e. the 'May monthly average' 0.17758953067863406 was computed from 25 of 31 days and has stood unchanged for three months.
rest.consequence: IICT Group's May-2026 consolidated P&L translates the HKD entity at an average that excludes the last six days of the month. The error is small (sub-1% on a normal HKD/AUD month) but it is invisible, permanent, and compounds with NFM-02: the same manual process that leaves months un-synced also freezes partial ones.
rest.remediation: Refuse to write a monthly_average for a month that has not fully elapsed (or write it with source='oxr_partial' and have the P&L translator treat it as missing), and have the cron proposed in NFM-02 re-derive the just-completed month so partial rows are overwritten with the full-month figure.

rest.title: full-year route reads monthly_report_settings and account_mappings with the raw client-supplied business_id while every other query uses the resolved dual-ID set
rest.evidence:
Line 150 resolves `const ids = await resolveBusinessProfileIds(supabase, business_id)`, and the forecast and actuals queries correctly use `.in('business_id', ids.all)` (lines 225, 261, 292). But two queries use the raw parameter:
- line 178: `.from('monthly_report_settings').select('*').eq('business_id', business_id).maybeSingle()`
- line 185: `.from('account_mappings').select('*').eq('business_id', business_id)`
Both return empty (not an error) on an id-space mismatch. The two tables live in opposite id-spaces from the actuals table this same route reads.

Downstream on empty mappings: `const category = mapping?.report_category || mapTypeToCategory(xero.account_type)` (line 350) silently reverts every account to the raw Xero type, and `mapping?.forecast_pl_line_id` / `forecast_pl_line_name` matching (lines 355-359) degrades to fuzzy-name-only. rest.title: An account with no budget renders '+0.0%' variance instead of 'no budget' — a misleading on-budget signal
rest.evidence:
calcVariance: `const percent = budget !== 0 ? (amount / Math.abs(budget)) * 100 : 0` (line 47) — the divide-by-zero is correctly guarded, but it returns the number 0, not null. The renderer DOES have a 'no data' path: `function fmtPct(value: number | null): string { if (value === null) return '—' ... }` (BudgetVsActualTable.tsx:26-29) — but the API never sends null, so it is unreachable for this case.

Recomputation for an unbudgeted opex account with actual $8,000, budget $0: amount = budget - actual = -8,000 (rendered red, correct); percent = 0 → fmtPct(0) → '+0.0%'. The row reads '-$8,000 / +0.0%'. Same pattern at full-year/route.ts:399 and 452, and generate/route.ts:527-530 (subtotals), 587, 591, 604, 608, 621, 627, 639.

Note also BudgetVsActualTable.tsx:33 `const favorable = isRevenue ? amount > 0 : amount > 0` — both ternary branches are identical (dead code). The colour happens to be correct because calcVariance already sign-normalises expenses, but the intent is not expressed.
rest.consequence: Every unbudgeted account in the client-facing monthly report shows a variance percentage of +0.0%, which reads as 'exactly on budget' next to a non-zero dollar variance. For a 'not a numbers person' this is the worst possible rendering of 'there is no budget for this line'.
rest.remediation: Return `percent: null` from calcVariance (and the sibling inline computations) when the budget is 0 and the actual is not, so the existing fmtPct(null) → '—' path fires. Widen the ReportLine type to `number | null` for the percent fields. Also collapse the dead ternary at BudgetVsActualTable.tsx:33 to `amount > 0` with a comment that calcVariance pre-normalises the sign.

rest.title: GST-on-OpEx uses a mis-derived gross-up formula when gst_applicable_expense_pct < 1
rest.evidence:
`monthGSTPaid += line.value * (gstRate * assumptions.gst_applicable_expense_pct / (1 + gstRate * assumptions.gst_applicable_expense_pct))` (line 576). The applicable percentage is folded into BOTH the numerator and the denominator of the gross-up fraction, which is not what 'a fraction p of this line is GST-inclusive at rate r' means.

Recomputation with gstRate = 0.1, gst_applicable_expense_pct = 0.8, line.value = $10,000:
- Code: 10,000 × (0.08 / 1.08) = $740.74
- Correct: 0.8 × 10,000 × (0.1 / 1.1) = $727.27
Overstatement $13.47 per $10k, i.e. 1.85% of the GST figure / 0.13% of the expense line. Contrast lines 567 and 570, which use the correct `gstRate / (1 + gstRate)` form for income and COGS.
rest.consequence: GST payable accrued in the cashflow forecast is slightly overstated for any client whose gst_applicable_expense_pct is below 1, biasing BAS payment timing and the projected bank balance downward by a fraction of a percent. Not material at current scale, but it is a genuine formula error sitting in a money path.
rest.remediation: Change to `line.value * assumptions.gst_applicable_expense_pct * (gstRate / (1 + gstRate))`. Add a unit test pinning the $10,000 / 0.8 / 10% case to $727.27.

rest.title: Two divergent balance-sheet stores: the 6-hourly xero_bs_lines mirror (7,792 rows) is unread by the app, imbalanced for 4 tenants, and invisible to the bs_equation invariant
rest.evidence:
Two stores exist: `xero_bs_lines` (long format, 7,792 rows, 14 tenants, business_profiles.id space, written 6-hourly by src/lib/xero/sync-orchestrator.ts:417) and `xero_balance_sheet_lines` (wide `monthly_values`, 383 rows, 11 real tenants, businesses.id space, written by src/lib/xero/bs-mirror-sync.ts via the 03:00 sync-bs-mirror cron).

Grep of src/ (excluding tests) shows `xero_bs_lines` has ZERO readers — only the orchestrator write at sync-orchestrator.ts:417 and audit scripts. The compat view `xero_bs_lines_wide_compat` also has zero readers (`xero_pl_lines_wide_compat` is read in ~12 routes; its BS twin in none). Everything client-facing reads either `xero_balance_sheet_lines` (src/lib/consolidation/balance-sheet.ts, src/lib/consolidation/cashflow.ts, metric-invariants) or live Xero (src/app/api/Xero/balance-sheet/route.ts).

  • xero_bs_lines imbalanced: Aeris Solutions 2026-08 −$70,539.88; Urban Road 2026-08 −$6,081.86 and 2026-07 +$9,328.41; Digital Bond 2026-06/07/08 +$2,384.81/+$2,406.20/+$3,906.20; Attaquer 2026-08 −$2,189.27. All of these read $0.00 in the wide store.

src/app/api/cron/metric-invariants/route.ts:122-124 reads `xero_balance_sheet_lines` for `bs_equation`, so none of the long-store imbalances are ever checked. metric_invariant_runs confirms: the only bs_equation failure in the last 3 days is Armstrong, and all other tenants report exactly 0.

Any new feature, ad-hoc query, or audit script (scripts/phase-70-data-audit.mjs already reads it) that reaches for xero_bs_lines picks up an Aeris balance sheet overstating current liabilities by $70,540. The BS-mirror trilogy fixes (#373/#376/#389) landed on the wide store; the long store never got them.
rest.remediation: Decide which store is canonical and delete or backfill the other. If xero_bs_lines is the intended future (it is the one the 6-hourly orchestrator writes and the one that balances exactly for Armstrong), point `bs_equation` at `xero_bs_lines_wide_compat` and move the readers; if `xero_balance_sheet_lines` is canonical, stop writing xero_bs_lines. Either way, extend `bs_equation` beyond the single newest month — the Armstrong 2026-05 failure and the Urban Road 2026-07 failure both sit outside the current month.

rest.title: Wages detail pulls payroll from one arbitrary Xero org for multi-org clients, while the P&L wages line covers all orgs
rest.evidence:
src/app/api/monthly-report/wages-detail/route.ts:316-321:
```
.from('xero_connections').select('*').in('business_id', ids.all).eq('is_active', true).limit(1).maybeSingle()
```
The `.limit(1)` avoids the PGRST116 null of FLEET-04 but instead picks ONE connection with no ORDER BY — PostgREST row order is unspecified, so which org is returned can vary between requests. That connection's tenant_id is then used for every PayCalendars / PayRuns / PayRun-detail call (route.ts:324-390) that builds the employee-level pay table. The same pattern repeats at route.ts:489-495 for the Sentry tenant tag.

Meanwhile the wages figure the tab reconciles against comes from `xero_pl_lines_wide_compat` (route.ts:154), which is summed across all of the business's tenants.

Affected in prod: Dragon Roofing (2 active connections) and IICT Group (3, one of them HKD).
rest.consequence: On the Wages tab for Dragon Roofing and IICT Group, the employee-level payroll breakdown covers only one of 2-3 Xero orgs while the P&L wages total covers all of them, so the detail never sums to the header. For IICT the arbitrarily-chosen org may be IICT Group Limited, in which case HKD payslip amounts are rendered against AUD P&L wages. Because there is no ORDER BY, the same report can show different employees on different loads.
rest.remediation: Use `resolveXeroConnections` and iterate all active connections, tagging each employee row with its source org (and translating non-AUD amounts through the same FX path as FLEET-01); or, if a single org is genuinely intended, add a deterministic `.order('display_order')` and label the tab with which org it covers.

rest.title: Three stale xero_connections rows attach all of IICT's Xero orgs to the internal "Wisdom BI" business

rest.title: monthly_report_snapshots: status/is_draft disagree on 3 of 6 rows, and one snapshot's stored revenue is $297k away from the mirror it was built from
rest.evidence:
SQL over all 6 monthly_report_snapshots rows: three have `status='draft'` while `is_draft=false` (Dragon Roofing 2026-07, Just Digital Signage 2026-04, Envisage 2026-03), i.e. the two draft flags contradict each other. Envisage 2026-01 has status='final', is_draft=false (consistent).

Comparing `summary->'revenue'->>'actual'` to the current xero_pl_lines revenue for the same business+month: Dragon Roofing 2026-07 1,230,584 vs 1,230,584 (match); Envisage 2026-04 101,667 vs 101,667 (match); Sharon King 2026-07 126,211 vs 126,617 (−406); Envisage 2026-03 62,035 vs 64,035 (−2,000); Envisage 2026-01 66,035 vs 68,035 (−2,000, and this one is status='final'); Just Digital Signage 2026-04 857,087 vs 560,265 (−296,822).

The Just Digital Signage April snapshot is $297k above the current mirror for that month, and Envisage's FINAL January report is $2,000 below — if a snapshot is ever re-served as the authoritative closed-month number it will not match what the P&L now says.

Separately, decide whether a snapshot is immutable evidence (in which case surface "as generated <date>; live data has since changed by $X") or a cache (in which case invalidate it when the underlying month re-syncs).

rest.title: Clean: orphans, duplicates, dual-ID fragmentation and impossible values across all 31 businesses
rest.evidence:
Orphans — swept all 96 non-deprecated tables with a uuid `business_id` column via query_to_xml, counting rows whose business_id matches neither businesses.id nor business_profiles.id. Result: 0 orphans everywhere except swot_analyses (17 of 18), and those 17 business_id values are confirmed auth.users ids (`count(*) filter (where exists (select 1 from auth.users u where u.id=s.business_id))` = 17) — the documented legacy owner-keying, not debris. businesses↔business_profiles is a clean 1:1 (31/31, no NULL or dangling business_id, no business without a profile).

Dual-ID fragmentation — for every one of those 96 tables, all populated rows sit in exactly ONE id-space; no table mixes businesses.id and business_profiles.id rows. The two id-spaces do not overlap.

Duplicates — checked xero_pl_lines (business+tenant+account_id+period+basis, and by account_code, and by account_name), xero_bs_lines (by account_id), subscription_budgets (business+vendor_key), business_kpis (business+kpi_id), subscription_vendor_actuals (business+tenant+vendor+month), weekly_metrics_snapshots, monthly_report_snapshots, financial_metrics, quarterly_snapshots: ZERO duplicate groups in all of them. The only "duplicate" hits were xero_bs_lines/xero_accounts grouped by account_code, and every one is account_code='' (bank accounts and credit cards, which have no code in Xero) — distinct account_ids, not real duplicates.

Month coverage — no gaps: all 13 active tenants have a contiguous run of xero_pl_lines months from first to last (26/26, 17/17, 14/14 etc.).

Impossible values — 0 negative or >$100k subscription_budgets.monthly_budget, 0 negative subscription_vendor_actuals, 0 |amount| > $50M in xero_pl_lines/xero_bs_lines, 0 rows where gross_profit ≠ revenue − cogs in financial_metrics, 0 margins outside ±100%, 0 conversion rates outside 0-100, 0 weekly snapshots with gross profit > revenue.

xero_bs_lines has a single `basis` value ('accruals') fleet-wide, so no cash/accrual double-count is possible there.
rest.consequence: None — this is the negative result. The classic orphan/duplicate/dual-ID failure modes the platform has historically produced are genuinely absent from prod today. Every material finding in this report is a freshness, cross-store or code-reads-the-wrong-thing problem, not row-level corruption.
rest.remediation: No action. Worth keeping the two sweeps (the query_to_xml orphan sweep and the per-table duplicate-key sweep) as a scripted check so a regression is caught, since neither is currently covered by metric_invariant_runs.

rest.title: 'Clear & Resync' deletes every Xero-derived forecast P&L line and then calls a shim route that no longer writes forecast_pl_lines — permanent loss reported as success
rest.evidence: handleClearAndResync (line 98) does `await supabase.from('forecast_pl_lines').delete().eq('forecast_id', forecastId).eq('is_from_xero', true)` (line 109-112, result never inspected), waits 500ms, POSTs /api/Xero/sync-forecast, and on `result.success` toasts 'Successfully cleared and resynced data from Xero!'. But src/app/api/Xero/sync-forecast/route.ts is now a shim whose own header states: 'Post-44: ... This shim delegates to the canonical orchestrator (refreshes xero_pl_lines for the business). It does NOT write to forecast_pl_lines.' The handler body confirms it — it only calls syncBusinessXeroPL(id). Prod holds 187 forecast_pl_lines rows with is_from_xero=true. Mitigating: the handler is threaded to XeroConnectionPanel via the onClearAndResync prop (finances/forecast/page.tsx:883, coach/clients/[id]/forecast/page.tsx:605) but XeroConnectionPanel.tsx renders no control bound to it, so the path is currently unreachable from the UI — hence MEDIUM, not CRITICAL. The sibling 'Sync from Xero' button IS rendered and toasts 'Successfully synced data from Xero!' after calling the same shim, which likewise writes nothing to forecast_pl_lines.
rest.consequence: Latent destructive path: the moment anyone re-adds the button (the prop is already wired on two pages, so it looks live to a reader), one click permanently deletes the Xero-sourced lines of a forecast — forecast_pl_lines has no soft-delete or archive — and the user is told it succeeded. Live today: the rendered 'Sync from Xero' button reports success for an operation that leaves the forecast page's data unchanged, training coaches to believe a refresh happened.
rest.remediation: Delete handleClearAndResync and the dead onClearAndResync prop, or reimplement it as a server route that deletes and repopulates in one transaction with checked errors. Retarget the 'Sync from Xero' toast to state what actually refreshed (Xero actuals), and check the delete's { error } wherever this pattern survives.

rest.title: Xero connection deactivation write is unchecked — Sentry can report 'connection deactivated' while the DB still says active
rest.evidence: After the terminal-error branch fires `Sentry.captureMessage('Xero connection deactivated', { tags: { invariant: 'xero_connection_deactivated' } })`, the actual state change is `await supabase.from('xero_connections').update({ is_active: false, updated_at: ... }).eq('id', connectionId);` (line 694-700) with no { error } destructuring — followed immediately by `return errorInfo`. The comment two lines above explicitly reasons about protecting 'the deactivation DB write that follows', but the write itself is unverified.
rest.consequence: If that update fails, the system has told Sentry the connection is dead and told the database nothing. The connection stays is_active=true, so it keeps being picked up by the sync rotation and keeps rendering as a live connection in the UI, while the refresh token is confirmed terminal — a connected-but-never-syncing state, which is the product's stated #1 incident class. releaseRefreshLock (line 913) is unchecked too, though LOCK_TTL_MS bounds that one.

Today it is bounded by fleet size (1-2 coaches, 1 run/week, last run 2026-08-23 20:01 status success), so impact is low. rest.title: Three crons have been permanently 'partial' for 15+ days, so the watchdog's 'degraded' alert has been continuously on and no longer distinguishes anything

A business can legitimately hold more than one active forecast: activate_forecast_locked (prod definition, verified via pg_get_functiondef) deactivates siblings only `WHERE business_id = … AND fiscal_year = … AND forecast_type = …`. Prod has 5 such businesses: Digital Bond, Distinct Directions, Envisage Australia, Just Digital Signage, Sydney Pressed Metal. rest.title: A $0.03 rounding delta permanently discards a whole month of balance-sheet rows and generates ~480 Sentry events in 16 days, burying real alerts
rest.evidence: sync_jobs for tenant e3671ec1 (Attaquer Pty Ltd), three most recent runs (2026-08-26 04:02, 2026-08-25 22:02, 2026-08-25 16:03) all identical: `reconciliation->'bs'` = {"months_failed":[], "months_fetched":14, "unbalanced_dates":[{"delta":0.03,"balance_date":"2026-07-31"}]}. sync-orchestrator.ts:363 gates on `Math.abs(delta) > 0.01`, and lines 382-383 (`for (const r of allRows) { if (!unbalancedSet.has(r.balance_date)) balancedRows.push(r) }`) drop EVERY row for that date. result.synthesis:
# WisdomBI Gap Report — post-forecast/security sweep, 26 Aug 2026

## 1. Executive verdict

**Not much is structurally rotten — but three things are producing wrong money on live client surfaces right now, and one of them is silent, unbounded, and gets worse every month.**

The four already-audited areas held up. Nothing in this sweep contradicts them. What the sweep found is that the audits were pointed at the *forecast* and the *access layer*, while the failures that survived are in the **multi-entity / multi-currency consolidation path** and in **pipeline-liveness state** — the two places where a number can be wrong without anything throwing.

**Dimensions that came back CLEAN (this is the real reassurance):**

- **Fleet data integrity** — a full-fleet sweep of 96 `business_id` columns across all 31 businesses found **zero orphans, zero duplicate keys, zero dual-ID fragmentation, zero impossible values** (FLEET-10). The dual-ID remediation is holding.
- **Secrets, client-bundle leakage** — all 1,736 commits swept for 14 credential shapes; **exactly one** real secret has ever been committed (SECR-01), and **zero** server secrets reach `.next/static` (10 patterns, 0 hits). No Xero, Anthropic, OpenAI, Resend, AWS or GitHub credential has ever been committed.
- **Reliability primitives** — Xero rate-limit handling (429 three-way split, `Retry-After`), sync idempotency (`begin_xero_sync_job` single-flight, 15-min bounded), partial-sync honesty (partials are never reported as success), and the cron house pattern on the three major per-item crons are all **correct**.
- **Cron scheduling** — all 8 crons on cadence, **0 failed runs and 0 dangling start-markers in 7 days**. The starvation class from #386 has not returned.
- **Client-facing presentation** — the public report at `/reports/view/[token]` is the best-behaved money surface in the app (gates on `has_budget`, shows dollars not percentages, states its own as-at date). Coach dashboard resolves both id-spaces correctly. Save paths are real API saves with debounce + `beforeunload` guards — no surviving legacy local-state-only handler.
- **Dependency risk** — 24 vulnerable packages triaged by reachability; only `next` is reachable (SECR-03). `jspdf`, `axios`, and 20 others provably are not.
- **NFM-05 was refuted outright** — the signed-denominator variance bug is real in the API but the only consumer `Math.abs()`es it and takes the sign from a correct field, so the rendered string is byte-identical to correct. Worth a one-line hardening, not a finding.

**The single most important remaining item: FLEET-01 / NFM-02 — HKD/AUD FX rates stopped on 25 May 2026 and nothing refreshes them.** IICT Group's revenue is being reported at **~5.3× reality** (July: $2,097,736 shown vs ~$398,616 actual; ~A$4.2M of phantom revenue across Jun/Jul/Aug) on the `/cfo` dashboard, the consolidated P&L, and the consolidated balance sheet. On the CFO dashboard specifically there is **no warning of any kind** — `fx_context.missing_rates` is computed correctly by `fx.ts` and then dropped by the caller at `src/app/api/cfo/summaries/route.ts:253-258`. IICT is `is_cfo_client = true`. The dashboard opens on July by default. There is no cron, no scraper, no invariant — the error grows by one month every month, forever, until someone manually clicks a button they have no reason to know exists. This is precisely the failure mode `fx.ts`'s own module doc says it was written to prevent.

The honest summary: **the platform's arithmetic is sound for the 16 single-entity, single-currency businesses. It is not sound for the two multi-entity ones, and it is not sound about whether its own data is current.**

---

## 2. Ranked action plan

### FIX NOW (this week — live wrong numbers or open credential exposure)

| # | Item | Change | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **FLEET-01 / NFM-02** — FX stale since 25 May, IICT ~5.3× overstated | (a) Enter HKD/AUD `monthly_average` + `closing_spot` for 2026-06/07/08 via the admin UI. (b) Thread `report.fx_context.missing_rates` into `ClientSummary` and render a warning chip on `/cfo`, suppressing the money figures when non-empty. (c) Add a monthly Vercel cron calling the OXR sync for the just-completed month, fail-loud to Sentry. (d) Add a `metric-invariants` check: active non-AUD tenant with P&L in a month lacking an `fx_rates` row = fail. | **data + code + config** |
